healthcareSystem: Basic public healthcare system largely funded by international aid. One main hospital in São Tomé city and a smaller one on Príncipe. Private healthcare options are minimal. Portuguese colonial-era infrastructure forms the backbone of the system.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is very basic. The Hospital Ayres de Menezes in São Tomé city is the main facility but lacks modern equipment and many specialists. Príncipe island has even fewer resources. Medical evacuation to Portugal, Gabon, or Angola is necessary for serious conditions.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies in São Tomé city open roughly 8am-6pm weekdays. Very limited hours on weekends. Few pharmacies outside the capital.
pharmacyTips: Bring all essential medications from home. Stock is unreliable and frequently out of basic items. Portuguese-speaking pharmacists. Verify expiry dates on all purchases. 'Farmácia' signs indicate licensed pharmacies.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is loose. Many medications sold without prescription when available. The main challenge is availability rather than regulations.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic painkillers
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. Carry a doctor's letter and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry prescription documentation from your physician.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in Portuguese or English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. Bring your entire supply — most medications are unavailable locally.

travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation coverage is essential. Serious conditions require evacuation to Lisbon, Libreville, or Luanda. Ensure malaria treatment and air ambulance are covered in your policy.

required: Yellow Fever (required if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
recommended: Malaria prophylaxis (essential — malaria is endemic throughout the islands)
vaccinations.notes: Malaria is a serious risk throughout both islands. Prophylaxis is strongly recommended. Yellow Fever certificate may be required depending on your origin country. Bring mosquito nets and repellent.

waterNotes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink. Use sealed bottled water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks. Bottled water is available in São Tomé city but may be harder to find in rural areas — carry a supply.
foodSafetyTips: Eat at established restaurants in São Tomé city. Fish and tropical fruit are staples — ensure fish is freshly cooked. Avoid raw salads and unpeeled fruit. Wash hands frequently. Food hygiene standards are basic.
medicalTourismNote: São Tomé and Príncipe is not a medical tourism destination. For any advanced medical needs, patients are evacuated to Portugal.
metaDescription: São Tomé and Príncipe health guide. Emergency contacts, malaria prevention, unsafe water, pharmacy tips, and medical evacuation advice.

hospitals.name: Hospital Ayres de Menezes
hospitals.notes: Main hospital on the island. Portuguese-speaking. Very basic equipment. Handles emergencies but capacity is limited.

hospitals.name: Hospital de Príncipe
hospitals.notes: Small hospital on Príncipe island. Extremely basic. For anything serious, transfer to São Tomé or evacuation is needed.

hospitals.name: São Tomé and Príncipe General Hospital
hospitals.notes: Government facility. Limited English. Bring a translator app.

dentalCare.availability: Extremely limited. A few dentists in São Tomé city only.
dentalCare.notes: Dental care is very basic. Only simple extractions and fillings available. No orthodontic or complex dental services.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Pack a dental emergency kit. For serious dental problems, evacuation to Portugal may be the only option.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: No dedicated mental health crisis line
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: None available. Mental health services are in Portuguese and extremely limited.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health infrastructure is virtually nonexistent. The country has very few trained mental health professionals. International NGOs provide some support.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility infrastructure does not exist. Roads are poor, buildings lack ramps, and terrain is hilly and uneven.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Shared taxis and hired vehicles are the only options.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Travelers with mobility challenges will face significant difficulties. A travel companion is essential. Most tourist sites are not accessible.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Very limited COVID testing available at the main hospital.
covidStatus.notes: COVID situation has stabilized. Healthcare capacity is extremely limited for any respiratory illness.

insuranceClaimProcess: Keep all receipts and documentation. Facilities require cash payment upfront (euros or local dobra accepted). Submit claims with itemized receipts to your insurer after returning home. Contact your insurer's emergency line immediately for potential evacuations.

commonCosts.note: Healthcare costs are low but quality is very basic. Cash payment required. Euros are widely accepted. Medical evacuation costs can exceed $40,000.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation is the only option for serious conditions. The international airport on São Tomé island is the departure point. Direct flights to Lisbon available. Ensure insurance covers evacuation.
